account.body: The first administrator. This happens once, and you stay signed in afterwards.
account.label: Your account
account.name: Your name
account.title: Create your account

connect.body: Point Adminium at a data source. We read the schema and never write to it unless you ask.

bridge.body: It was handed over from adminium.dev. Create your account and we will open it in the connect wizard, where you can read it before anything uses it.
bridge.title: A connection string is waiting for this instance

dsn.helper: Nothing leaves this browser until your account exists — then we test it.
dsn.incomplete: Add the host and database, e.g. postgres://user@host:5432/db
dsn.invalidScheme: Unrecognized scheme — expected postgres://, mysql://, mariadb:// or sqlite:
dsn.label: Connection string

existing.body: It holds {count, plural, one {# Adminium table} other {# Adminium tables}} with data in them. Two things you can do:
existing.failed: Could not point this instance at that database.
existing.otherSecret: It was set up with a different ADMINIUM_SECRET: signing in there would work, but its saved connection strings cannot be decrypted by this instance.

parked.body: They are renamed out of the way — every row survives — and Adminium starts with fresh ones beside them. Nothing happens until you choose to put Adminium’s own data in this database.
parked.title: The tables that are there will be kept

existing.timeout: Adminium is pointed at that database but has not come back yet — reload this page in a moment.
existing.title: That database already runs an Adminium

connect.label: Connect data
connect.title: Connect your database

connected.reading: Connected — Adminium is reading your schema now.
connected.tables: Connected · {count, plural, one {# table} other {# tables}} found.

done.invited: {count, plural, one {# invitation} other {# invitations}} created.
done.label: All set

next.blank: Your workspace is ready. Add a page whenever you are — nothing was generated, exactly as you asked.
next.generate: Your workspace is ready. Next we will pick the tables to include and generate your pages.

storage.local: Adminium keeps its own data in a file on this machine.
storage.sameDb: Adminium keeps its own data in the database you connected.
storage.separate: Adminium keeps its own data in the database you gave it.

done.title: You’re all set! 🎉

error.alreadyCompleted: This instance has already been set up. Sign in with the existing admin account.
error.connectionFailed: Your account was created and you are signed in — but that database could not be reached: {detail}
error.failed: Setup failed. Check your connection and try again.
error.rejected: The server rejected those details. Check the email and password and try again.

meta.body: Your login, the pages you generate and your saved settings. That is separate from the database you just connected, which Adminium only reads.
meta.label: Adminium’s data

local.body: Nothing to set up. Right for trying Adminium out, or for a single instance.
local.title: In a file on this machine

moving.failed: Could not move Adminium’s data — retry.
moving.timeout: Adminium moved its data but has not come back yet. It is safe in the new database — reload this page in a moment.

pinned.body: This instance was started with its meta store configured, so there is nothing to move. You can change it later from Studio settings.
pinned.title: Adminium’s data already has a home

sameDb.alreadyAdminium: That database already holds an Adminium instance. Go back a step to keep its tables and start beside them, or sign in to it instead.
sameDb.body: Adminium adds its own `adminium_` tables beside yours. One database to back up.
sameDb.disabledFile: A SQLite file is not a server Adminium can add its own tables to.
sameDb.disabledNoDdl: That role cannot run CREATE TABLE, which Adminium’s own migrations need.
sameDb.disabledReadOnly: That role is read-only — Adminium never writes to your database. Keep its data in a file, or give it one of its own.
sameDb.noSource: You have not connected a database yet — connect one first, or keep Adminium’s data in a file.
sameDb.parked: The Adminium tables already in there are renamed out of the way first — every row survives — and Adminium starts with fresh ones beside them.
sameDb.title: In the database you just connected

separate.body: A PostgreSQL or MySQL database you provide. Right for production, or for several instances.
separate.incomplete: Add the host and database, e.g. postgres://user@host:5432/adminium
separate.insufficient: That role cannot run CREATE TABLE — Adminium’s own migrations need it.
separate.invalidScheme: Unrecognized scheme — expected postgres://, mysql:// or mariadb://
separate.label: Connection string for Adminium
separate.ok: Reachable, and it can create tables.
separate.title: In a database of its own

meta.title: Where Adminium keeps its own data

start.body: This only shapes the pages we generate for you. You can change any of it later, or start from nothing.
start.label: Starting point

analytics.body: Charts and tables to read. Nothing writes back.
analytics.title: Read-only analytics

blank.body: Generate nothing. Connect a database and build the pages you want, one at a time.
blank.title: Blank canvas

crud.body: Tables and forms, without the dashboards.
crud.title: CRUD tables

fullAdmin.body: A page per table, with create, edit and delete.
fullAdmin.title: Full admin panel

support.body: Queues and customer detail pages first, with deletes off.
support.title: Support console

start.title: What will you build first?

team.body: Invite the people you work with. You can always add more later.
team.duplicate: That person has already been invited.
team.failed: That invitation could not be created.
team.label: Your team
team.note: Invitations without email show a link you send yourself. It is shown once — Adminium keeps only a hash of it.
team.title: Bring your team
